name: North Orange County Chamber

whyTheyFit: This is the merged Fullerton and Buena Park chamber and its own site lists member directories for Anaheim, Brea, Buena Park, Cypress, Fullerton, La Habra, La Palma, Orange and Stanton, which means one after-hours mixer here puts the venue in front of manufacturers, dealerships, dental practices and school districts from every other lane on this board at the same time, and the room turns over monthly so the introduction repeats without being re-sold.
buyingWindow: Sep-Nov to get onto the following year's mixer rota, plus Jan when the annual event slate is set
headcountBasis: Modeled on typical attendance at a multi-city chamber's monthly evening mixer, not on the membership roll. Estimate only. The referral value is far larger than this number and is not counted in it.

name: Korean American Chamber of Commerce of Orange County
orgTypeBasis: Its own contact page dates the organisation to 1978 and prints one Buena Park suite address and one general mailbox, with no parent body named.
address: 6281 Beach Blvd Ste 345, Buena Park, CA 90621
whyTheyFit: This chamber has organised Korean American business owners across Orange County since 1978 from a suite on Beach Blvd, and its members are overwhelmingly the owner-operated restaurants, dental practices, insurance agencies and import firms that sit in the same Brea and Fullerton strip centres this board already walks, so a single introduction here reaches a network of small employers who buy staff nights personally and quickly rather than through a procurement cycle.
buyingWindow: Jan-Feb around Lunar New Year gatherings, plus Sep-Nov for the year-end banquet
headcountBasis: Modeled on a single-ethnicity county chamber's mixer and year-end banquet attendance. Estimate only.
note: Referral partner rather than buyer. Worth pairing with the Korean-owned businesses already researched in the retail and food lane, since the chamber is the shortest route to all of them at once.
addressSource: Organisation's own contact page at kaccoc.org, read 14 Aug 2026

name: Fullerton Marriott at California State University
orgTypeBasis: A Marriott-branded full-service property with a Marsha code and a brand.com property page, so it is operated inside a chain and carries a brand sales structure.
decisionMakerTitle: Director of Sales & Marketing / Group Sales Manager
whyTheyFit: This hotel sits on the edge of the Cal State Fullerton campus and its own events page publishes 9,838 square feet across nine rooms with a 320-seat Grand Ballroom, which means the group business it lands is conference, athletics and university-adjacent groups who arrive with three nights to fill and only one banquet, so its sales team is asked what to do on the other two evenings by people who have already committed a budget.
buyingWindow: Year-round for group referrals; Nov-Dec for its own associate holiday party
headcountBasis: Range is the hotel's own associate holiday or recognition party for a full-service property of this size, which is the only thing it would buy for itself. Estimate only. The referred group business is not counted in this number.
note: Simultaneously a competitor. With a 320-seat ballroom and its own catering operation it sells the exact banquet a corporate prospect might otherwise buy from the venue, so the honest pitch is the off-site evening the hotel cannot supply rather than the dinner it can.
addressSource: Marriott.com property events page for LAXFL, read 14 Aug 2026
